name: Grand Lake St. Marys
story: Grand Lake St. Marys has experienced severe toxic algal blooms. EPA research has identified phosphorus input from agricultural runoff as a primary driver.
sts_angle: A compact case where water-quality crisis triggered nutrient-management rules, conservation programs, and conflict over agricultural practices.
source: U.S. EPA — Grand Lake St. Marys phosphorus and agricultural drainage report

name: Lower Green Bay
story: Harmful algal blooms are common in lower Green Bay. Excess nutrients from agricultural and urban runoff interact with a long industrial pollution legacy.
sts_angle: Useful for showing that a waterbody can carry overlapping agricultural, urban, and industrial histories rather than one simple pollution story.
source: U.S. EPA — Lower Green Bay/Fox River Area of Concern

name: Upper Mississippi River — Pool 8 backwaters
story: Backwaters around Navigation Pool 8 near La Crosse have been studied for cyanobacteria, cyanotoxins, and excessive plant and algal growth. Nutrient availability is one factor influencing cyanobacterial abundance and toxicity.
sts_angle: This puts an ecological consequence directly inside the Mississippi system and shows how river engineering, backwater connectivity, nutrient loading, and monitoring interact.
source: U.S. Geological Survey — Upper Mississippi River cyanobacteria research

name: Cheney Reservoir
story: Cheney Reservoir is Wichita's primary drinking-water supply and has a long history of cyanobacterial blooms and taste-and-odor events studied alongside nutrient and sediment loading.
sts_angle: Shows how agricultural watershed management becomes tied directly to municipal drinking-water treatment and long-term monitoring infrastructure.
source: U.S. Geological Survey — Cheney Reservoir and Water Quality Studies

name: Lake Okeechobee
story: Lake Okeechobee experiences large cyanobacterial blooms in a nutrient-rich and heavily managed lake system, with consequences extending into connected canals and estuaries.
sts_angle: A strong case for studying nutrient legacies, engineered water flows, agriculture, restoration, and contested responsibility.
source: Florida DEP — Harmful Algal Bloom Assessment of Lake Okeechobee System

name: Upper Klamath Lake
story: Upper Klamath Lake regularly experiences cyanobacterial blooms; Oregon health officials issue recreational advisories when blooms or cyanotoxins pose exposure concerns.
sts_angle: A western case where ecological monitoring sits inside a larger system of irrigation, fisheries, water allocation, and environmental governance.
